summary: In Hermes Agent, on a normal step the configured main model proposes tool calls or a text answer; code checks an answer before accepting it and can send the model back, for example up to twice for a short reply that only announces a next step. Code applies the limits, among them a step allowance per turn, automatic compression as the prompt nears the window, and an optional time budget that can warn near the end but does not itself stop the run.

judgments.question: May this sender's message dispatch agent work?
judgments.answer: Code walks a fixed order of grants on every incoming gateway message. On a fresh install with no allowlist, an unknown sender is refused unless an operator approved their pairing code.

judgments.question: The reply ends by announcing a next action but makes no tool call: is the model stalled?
judgments.answer: On by default when tools are offered. A reply of at most 400 characters with no tool call that ends on an announced next step ("I'll now", "next, I") is treated as a stall and the model is nudged to act, at most twice per turn, a limit shared with two similar checks.

judgments.question: Has this turn used up its step allowance?
judgments.answer: Code normally takes one step from the turn's allowance as each loop iteration starts. The cap is agent.max_turns: 500 in the config.yaml the installers seed, 150 after the recommended hermes setup, 90 after Blank Slate setup, and no cap with no finite value; a delegated child defaults to 250. At the cap the turn ends, apart from one granted grace call.

judgments.question: Should the model be told to wrap up because the wall-clock budget is 80% gone?
judgments.answer: Off by default. With a run budget set, after 80% of the time has passed code adds a one-time wrap-up notice to a tool result when it can. The setting does not itself stop the run when the time is up.

judgments.question: Should automatic compression run now?
judgments.answer: On by default. Code compresses once the prompt passes a threshold worked out from the usable input window (by default starting from 50%, raised to at least 75% for windows under 512K tokens); floors, caps, deferral and failure safeguards can move or block it.

judgments.question: Who writes the summary that replaces the middle of the conversation?
judgments.answer: A language model, in one auxiliary compression request that sets no max_tokens. Empty, refused or cut-off replies count as failures.

judgments.question: What should the agent do next: call which tools with which arguments, or answer?
judgments.answer: On a normal model call, the main model proposes tool calls or a text answer. Before a call can run, code repairs or rejects a tool name it does not know and checks that the arguments are valid JSON; other guards can still stop a call.

judgments.question: Retries and fallbacks are spent on a passing outage: wait, or end the turn?
judgments.answer: On by default. For an overload, server error or timeout, and only if no answer text has reached the user, code waits with a visible countdown, about 15, 30, then 60 seconds (or the provider's own Retry-After, up to 120 seconds), and stops after five cycles.

problems.title: A run budget can warn near the end but does not enforce a deadline
problems.plain: With --run-budget or agent.run_budget_seconds set, once 80% of the time has passed Hermes adds a one-time wrap-up notice to a tool result when it can, and it can shorten a default wait on a silent model call. The setting does not itself stop the run when the time is up, although the option's help text says it is intended for runs with a hard ceiling. An open pull request proposes stopping the model at the deadline.

verified.claimsPass: an independent AI reviewer from another company (OpenAI Codex, read-only) on 2026-11-08, in three rounds; every sentence it found too wide was narrowed or removed

problems.title: Subagent calls over the limit in one reply are dropped without telling the model
problems.plain: When a model reply has passed Hermes' tool-call checks and asks for more delegate_task calls than delegation.max_concurrent_children (10 by default), Hermes drops the calls over the limit before the reply goes into the conversation. The cap itself only logs a warning, and the model gets no result for the dropped calls. An open report in Hermes' tracker describes this.

problems.title: A /loop ends when its finishing line appears anywhere in a reply
problems.plain: A /loop ends as done when a reply has a line that is only LOOP_COMPLETE. The check matches such a line anywhere in the reply, not only at the end as the function's own description says, so a reply with that line in the middle also ends the loop.
